qt: to the Commission Piotr Müller (ECR) Subject:

According to data from the Polish Ministry of Development and Technology, employment in the furniture industry fell from 165 000 in 2022 to 133 000 in August 2026. In the first seven months of 2026, exports of Polish furniture fell by 3.8%, while imports of furniture from China grew by nearly 20% by weight. EU product and chemical safety requirements apply equally to furniture from third countries, but their effectiveness depends on customs controls and market surveillance. In this connection: 1.

Is the Commission monitoring imports of furniture from China for dumping or a surge in volume, and is it considering initiating anti-dumping or safeguard proceedings, and if so, within what timeframe?
Will the Commission include furniture imported from third countries, including when sold online, in the coordinated control activities of customs and market surveillance authorities, and if so, when?

How will the Commission ensure that furniture manufacturers in Poland and across the EU enjoy a level playing field when competing with imports from third countries, and will it assess their total costs before imposing further obligations on the industry?
